key_insight: In three-sphere ball-milling collisions, geometry and friction govern particle trapping, while impact conditions and particle size ratio determine fracture.
engineering_relevance: These results can inform ball-milling configurations that favor particle capture and breakage.
method: Simulate a minimal three-sphere collision geometry using the discrete element method (DEM).
Describe trapping with a closed-form geometric condition incorporating friction.
Evaluate fracture from DEM output using Christensen-type stress and Weibull-type contact-force normalized criteria.
evidence_signal: The numerical study finds that critical fracture conditions vary with impact angle, obliquity, velocity, and size ratio; head-on collisions with larger size ratios require lower critical impact velocities.
watch_item: The minimal three-sphere model may not capture the many-body interactions and operating variability of a full ball mill.
paper_title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
